title: A lever and a reward
hook: Actions can be followed by consequences.

knows: Animals can respond to cues and conditions.
doesNotKnow: In a toy trial, food follows a lever press. Which before-and-later counts would show an increase in pressing?

misconception: The stated evidence implies a different interpretation or a universal conclusion.
objective: In a toy trial, food follows a lever press. Which before-and-later counts would show an increase in pressing?

claims.text: In a toy trial, food follows a lever press. Which before-and-later counts would show an increase in pressing? The stipulated record shows one press before and four after the rewarded action. It illustrates a change in action frequency after a consequence; without further controls this tiny record does not establish why the change occurred.

claims.text: The panels show a stipulated illustrative model and do not depict observed data.
A toy animal performs an action twice before a reward and five times later. What does the record compare? The stated counts compare how often the action occurs.
